land.text: Persia and the Caucasus, held by the empire's governors since the 1230s and given to Hulagu in 1251-1256

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Mongol Empire row covers the ulus until 1293.

land.text: the whole Hulaguid ulus under Gaykhatu

successors.note: Same state; the 1293/1294 break is Cliopatria's bookkeeping.

capitals.name: Maragheh
capitals.note: Infobox 'Maragheh (1258-1265)'; the Hulagu page mentions Maragheh only for the observatory he patronised. Hulagu chose Azerbaijan as his power base.

capitals.name: Tabriz
capitals.note: Infobox 'Tabriz (1265-1307)'; Soltaniyeh from 1306 is outside this dossier.

rulers.name: Hulagu
rulers.title: Ilkhan
rulers.note: The Hulagu page gives no reign dates; 1256 is the infobox date of the Ilkhanate as a region of the empire (Ilkhan from 1258), and he died on 8 February 1265 on the Zarrineh River.

rulers.name: Abaqa
rulers.note: Succeeded Hulagu in the summer of 1265 (Ilkhanate page).

rulers.name: Gaykhatu
rulers.note: Reigned 1291-1295; the reign continues in the ilkhanate dossier.

correction.text: Persia and Azerbaijan under Hulagu: Möngke 'appointed Hulagu to administer the Middle East'; the Assassins surrendered Alamut early in 1256

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row (the Mongol Empire row covers all). The pages name the Middle East and Persia, not a boundary: Iran, Azerbaijan, Transcaucasia and Khorasan are the researcher's reading. The Qara'unas Mongols ruled Khorasan as an autonomous realm that paid no taxes (Ilkhanate page).

correction.text: as 1256 plus Mesopotamia after the fall of Baghdad on 10 February 1258

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Baghdad surrendered on 10 February and the Mongols entered on 13 February 1258 (Hulagu page); Syria is an occupation of 1260, not drawn here.

correction.text: Cliopatria's Ilkhanate shape of 1294 without Anatolia, which is drawn as the vassal Sultanate of Rum: 'For the remainder of the 13th century, the Seljuks acted as vassals of the Ilkhanate'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Cliopatria's 1294 Ilkhanate shape is 3.77 M km2 against the infobox 3.75 M km2 for 1310 (ratio 1.0); removing Anatolia leaves about 3.0 M km2. The shape also contains the Caucasus vassals (Georgia, Armenia), which the vassal events tint. The pages date no border change on the Ilkhanid side between 1260 and 1293 except the Anatolian status, so the shape is held constant; Syria is lost with Ain Jalut in 1260.

region.text: Persia, Azerbaijan, the Caucasus and Khorasan under Hulagu

ledger.note: 1256: Hulagu's Persia stands as a region of the Mongol Empire. Infobox 'Administrative region of Mongol Empire (1256-1259)'; Hulagu's campaign began in 1256 'when the Nizari Ismaili state was destroyed', and he reached Transoxiana in 1255; he was appointed by Möngke, 'installed as Great Khan in 1251'.

region.text: Alamut and the Nizari Ismaili strongholds in Daylam

ledger.note: 1256: the Ismaili state falls. 'The Assassins surrendered Alamut without a fight' in early 1256 (Hulagu page); the Ilkhanate page: the campaign 'began in 1256, when the Nizari Ismaili state was destroyed'. Girdkuh held out to 1271 (mongol-empire dossier).

region.text: the Kingdom of Georgia, East and West

ledger.note: 1256: Georgia is a vassal of the Mongol Great Khan, inherited from the empire: David VII's coin read 'David, son of Giorgi, Bagrationi, vassal of the Mongol Great Khan Mangu'; the Georgian crown is divided East and West from 1247. The page does not name the Ilkhanate for the 1250s; the mongol-empire dossier dates the submission to 1243.

1256: the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia is a Mongol vassal. The Hulagu page lists 'the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia under Hethum I' among his vassals without a date; the Ilkhanate page has Cilicia submitting to the Great Khan. Inherited date.
1256: the Empire of Trebizond is a Mongol vassal. The Ilkhanate page: 'the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum and the Empire of Trebizond became Mongol vassals after 1243'. Inherited date.

region.text: the Sultanate of Rum and Anatolia

ledger.note: October 1256: all Anatolia is subject. 'In October 1256, Bayju defeated Kaykaus II near Aksaray and all of Anatolia became officially subject to Möngke Khan'; 'For the remainder of the 13th century, the Seljuks acted as vassals of the Ilkhanate'. Rum had been a Mongol vassal since Köse Dağ (1243).

region.text: Baghdad and the caliphate's last lands in Iraq

ledger.note: 29 January 1258: the siege of Baghdad opens. 'The siege began on 29 January 1258' after the army set out in November 1257.

region.text: Baghdad and the caliphate's last lands in Iraq

ledger.note: 10 February 1258: Baghdad surrenders. Baghdad surrendered on 10 February and the Mongols entered on 13 February; the Ilkhanate page: 'The Abbasid Caliphate was destroyed, and Hulagu proclaimed himself ilkhan'.

region.text: Baghdad and the caliphate's last lands in Iraq

ledger.note: February 1258: Mesopotamia is Hulagu's. The Abbasid Caliphate is destroyed with the sack of Baghdad (10-13 February 1258); Maragheh becomes the capital this year (infobox 1258-1265).
1260: Hulagu's army takes Aleppo. 'Aleppo was captured by siege in 1260' (the page gives no month; the mongol-empire dossier has January).
1 March 1260: Damascus falls. 'Damascus was seized on 1 March 1260'.

September 1260: the Mamluks retake Damascus. Ain Jalut was fought 'on 3 September 1260'; 'the Mamluks captured Damascus five days later after Ain Jalut'; 'The battle of Ain Jalut established a high-water mark for the Mongol conquest' (Hulagu page).
October 1260: the Mamluks retake Aleppo 'within a month' of Ain Jalut; 'They never returned to Syria again' (Ain Jalut page).

region.text: the Caucasus: the Derbend pass and the Terek

ledger.note: 1262: the Berke–Hulagu war. Berke declared war in 1262 (Ilkhanate page); Hulagu 'marched north through the Derbend pass and was ambushed on the Terek by Nogai's army' (Berke–Hulagu page). The Hulagu page has the defeat in 1263.
1265: Hulagu (8 February) and Berke both die; no peace and no frontier change is recorded.
1293: bookkeeping end of the ulus; Rum remains an Ilkhanid vassal until Mesud II is murdered in 1308 (Rum page).
1293: bookkeeping end of the ulus; Georgia stays under the Ilkhanate until 1335 (Georgia page: Shaykh Hasan appointed governor in 1334; civil war in the Ilkhanate 1335).
1293: bookkeeping end of the ulus; Cilicia stays an Ilkhanid vassal in the ilkhanate dossier.
1293: bookkeeping end of the ulus; Trebizond stays a vassal in the later dossiers.

1293: the Hulaguid ulus carries on as the Ilkhanate. A bookkeeping break: the Ilkhanate page treats 1256 (region of the empire) to 1335 as one state under Hulagu, Abaqa, Tegüder, Arghun, Gaykhatu; Cliopatria's Ilkhanate row begins in 1294.

wars.name: Mongol conquest of the Nizari Ismailis
wars.outcome: Alamut was surrendered 'without a fight' in early 1256; the other strongholds fell the same year (Girdkuh held out to 1271).
wars.note: No contest zone: the strongholds were taken in a campaign without a front.

wars.name: Siege of Baghdad (1258)
wars.outcome: The army left in November 1257, the siege began on 29 January 1258, the city surrendered on 10 February and was entered on 13 February; the Abbasid Caliphate ended.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Syria and Ain Jalut
wars.outcome: Aleppo fell in 1260 and Damascus on 1 March; after Ain Jalut the Mongols lost Syria, 'a high-water mark for the Mongol conquest'.

wars.name: Berke–Hulagu war
wars.outcome: Hulagu was routed on the Terek in 1262 (1263 on the Hulagu page); Hulagu and Berke died in 1265; no frontier change recorded.

wars.name: Mamluk–Ilkhanid wars (to 1293)
wars.outcome: The Mamluks beat Ilkhanid forces at Elbistan in Anatolia in 1277 ('Baibars raided Anatolia and defeated the Mongols') and Möngke Temür was beaten at Homs in 1281; no border change is dated on these pages.
wars.note: Elbistan, 1277: the Rum page has the Mamluks 'temporarily replacing them as administrator of the realm'; Abaqa executed the regent Parwana (Ilkhanate page).

certainty.note: Mountain, desert and steppe frontiers; the Euphrates line with the Mamluks and the Caucasus line with the Golden Horde are zones of campaigns, not surveyed lines.

sources.title: Ilkhanate
sources.note: Infobox: administrative region of the Mongol Empire 1256-1259, independent khanate 1260-1335; capitals Maragheh 1258-1265, Tabriz 1265-1307; 3.75 M km2 (1310); Berke 1262; Abaqa 1265-82; Elbistan 1277; Homs 1281; khans to 1295.

sources.title: Hulagu Khan
sources.note: Hulagu: Alamut surrendered early 1256; Baghdad 29 Jan to 13 Feb 1258; Aleppo 1260; Damascus 1 March 1260; Ain Jalut 1260; defeat north of the Caucasus; death 8 February 1265; vassals Cilicia and Georgian volunteers.

sources.title: Sultanate of Rum
sources.note: Rum: Kose Dag 1243, Aksaray October 1256 (all Anatolia subject to Mongke), vassals of the Ilkhanate, Elbistan 1277, Mesud II murdered 1308.

sources.title: Kingdom of Georgia
sources.note: Georgia: vassal of the Mongol Great Khan (coin of David VII); East and West division 1247-1329; Mongol governors; reunification 1329.

sources.title: Battle of Ain Jalut
sources.note: Ain Jalut on 3 September 1260; Damascus retaken five days later, Aleppo within a month; the Mongols never returned to Syria.

notes:
The Hulaguid ulus before Cliopatria's Ilkhanate row (1294): the ilkhanate dossier says its 1256-1293 phase is not drawn separately and starts at 1294 to match the mongol-empire dossier, which ends in 1293. This dossier is that phase. No Cliopatria shape exists, so the three keyframes are new; the last (1260-1293) reuses the Ilkhanate 1294 shape minus Anatolia, which the pages show as the vassal Sultanate of Rum.

Dates that disagree: Hulagu's defeat north of the Caucasus is 1262 (Ilkhanate and Berke-Hulagu pages) or 1263 (Hulagu page); the Ilkhanate infobox gives independence in 1260 but 'the ilkhan' title in 1258; Alamut 'early 1256' (Hulagu page) vs the November/December date of the mongol-empire dossier. The Hulagu page does not give Maragheh as a capital (infobox of the Ilkhanate page does: 1258-1265).

Overlaps with the mongol-empire dossier: it already records the Baghdad (1258), Aleppo and Damascus (1260), Ismaili (1257), Rum and Georgia (1243) events as the Mongol Empire's. Here they are the Hulaguid ulus's own; the orchestrator should decide which dossier the renderer uses 1256-1293 (the ulus is inside the Mongol Empire row throughout). The Georgia, Cilicia and Trebizond vassal events are confidence 1 (inherited from 1243, dates not on the pages opened). Not drawn: the Qara'unas (Negudaris) of Khorasan, autonomous and tax-free (Ilkhanate page), and the Georgian East/West division of 1247 (Georgia page); Kaidu's raids into Khorasan from 1288 (see ogedeid-ulus); Mamluk attacks in Anatolia in 1277.

Counterparts needing dossiers: nizari-ismaili-state (flagged by ia-02-a to me-08/me-09), ayyubid-sultanate (Cliopatria row; me-09), ulus-of-jochi and ulus-of-chagatai (this batch), abbasid-caliphate (me-08).
